raw_response.country: United States (foreign assistance policy targeting developing countries globally)

criterion_notes.c1: The paper addresses access to safe drinking water and sanitation in developing countries as an objective of the US Paul Simon Water for the Poor Act of 2005.
criterion_notes.c2: Passes the plain wording of Criterion 2 (plain=yes) because it examines a statutory and governance framework, namely the US Paul Simon Water for the Poor Act of 2005 (PL 109-121), USAID/State Department implementation, and Integrated Water Resources Management. However, it fails the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading (narrow=no) because the Act is a macro-level US foreign assistance and project-funding policy framework rather than a rule-type legal or administrative mechanism directly governing household or community service access (such as eligibility rules, tenure/documentation requirements, tariff/cost-recovery rules, enforcement, or utility regulation). Regardless, plain_criterion2_decision is still exclude because the paper lacks empirical evidence (c3=no).
criterion_notes.c3: No empirical evidence or systematic synthesis is presented. The paper is a policy overview and prospective methodological proposal describing how GIS and triangulation will be used in future work to assess WfP Act projects, explicitly noting that spatial parameters are still needed in order to begin spatial analysis; Table 1 merely reproduces descriptive regional baseline coverage statistics from the 2008 Report to Congress.
criterion_notes.c4: No empirical service-access outcomes of the policy or projects are measured or analysed; the paper states prospectively that project outcomes will be classified and linked to MDG Joint Monitoring Programme data in a future GIS analysis, while Table 1 only reprints aggregate regional baseline water and sanitation percentages from a government report.
criterion_notes.c5: Because the proposed GIS and triangulation assessment had not yet been conducted, there is no completed empirical study design, sample, or measured exposure-outcome analysis.

evidence_quotes.quote: This paper outlines a methodology to assess the Paul Simon Water for the Poor Act (WfP Act) by (1) tracking access to safe water and sanitation, (2) identifying water resources governance and management efforts for water productivity, and (3) including efforts to improve water security through increased cooperation on shared waters.

The Act makes access to water and sanitation in developing countries an explicit foreign policy objective of the US government, requiring the Secretary of State and the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) with other US agencies to implement policies.

Baseline data on physical, ecological, political, and social boundaries will be organized into a geographic information system and organized into a nested spatial hierarchy reflecting local, regional, and global scales.

Defining the spatial parameters of these projects – areas impacted that include not only demographics, but also the associated environments, ecosystems, and water systems are needed in order to begin the process of spatial analysis.

raw_response.exposure: Paul Simon Water for the Poor Act of 2005 (PL 109-121) US foreign assistance policy and water/sanitation programs
raw_response.rationale: Excluded under E05 (No empirical evidence). This conference paper provides a policy overview of the US Paul Simon Water for the Poor Act of 2005 and outlines a prospective GIS and triangulation methodology to track future project outcomes, explicitly stating that defining spatial parameters is still needed in order to begin spatial analysis and reporting only reproduced regional baseline figures from the 2008 State Department Report to Congress. In addition, under the narrow 2026-10-13 Criterion 2 clarification, the Act is a macro-level foreign aid and project-delivery framework rather than a rule-type legal/administrative mechanism directly governing household or community service access; under both plain and narrow readings of Criterion 2, the paper is excluded for lack of empirical evidence.
raw_response.study_design: Policy overview and proposed GIS/triangulation methodological framework (non-empirical)
